title: C1186 — Fuel injector 6 connector
introduction:
The injector meters fuel, but this page follows the electrical connections that belong to it. I keep the housing identity and circuit identity together: recognizing the plug’s silhouette is only half the introduction.

Use the opening table to identify the connector, then carry each printed cavity label from the drawing into its assignment row. Read the row across to see the circuit identifier, wire description, function and terminal listing. The pigtail table completes the reference by separating the service assembly from its engineering shell.

This map does not establish injector operation. Physical viewing direction, access, electrical testing and replacement need matching vehicle documentation. Engine applicability and the conventions behind Gauge, Size and Used are unspecified here; retain them as reference entries rather than inferring injection type or choosing repair wire.

edits.why: I use the latch at the top of the drawing and the vertically stacked cavities to keep my place. Their printed labels provide the link to the assignment rows below. Check the identity table and shell-and-harness row when reading the illustration together. The drawing’s upright layout does not establish which side of a physical connector faces the viewer.

Each row keeps a cavity, circuit identifier, wire description, function and terminal identifier together. The Function column separates the injector-driver connection from the supply connection, whose description retains fuse or circuit-breaker alternatives. I preserve the driver entry’s polarity sign as part of its label; it is not enough to infer a switching strategy, expected voltage or fault. Those questions belong to the matching diagnostic procedure.

Match Kit List above to Number here to find the catalogued connector-and-wire assembly. Service Part identifies that assembly, and Engineering Shell links it to the housing identity. Neither should be confused with the terminal identifier in the circuit table. The pigtail’s Gauge field and the assignment table’s Gauge field describe their respective entries; they do not supply a wire-substitution or splicing instruction.
